pass_a_gloss: Thrones and hundredfold; Origen wishes children/fields to leave; martyrs as fathers of fathers.
pass_b_english: As Peter once said to the Savior, 'Behold, we left all and followed thee; what then shall we have?' (Matthew 19:27–29) And Jesus said to them — plainly to the apostles — 'Amen, I say to you: you who followed me, in the regeneration, when God sits on his throne of glory, you too shall sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. And everyone who left brothers or sisters or parents or children or fields or houses for my name's sake shall receive manifold, and inherit eternal life.' For the sake of these words, I would have prayed — possessing on earth as much as you, Ambrose, and more — to become a witness in Christ God, to 'receive manifold' — or as Mark says, 'hundredfold.' For a hundredfold is far more than the few we leave, if we go to martyrdom, with them hundredfolded. For this, if I bear witness, I wished to leave children too, with fields and houses — that with God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, 'from whom every family in the heavens and on earth is named,' (Mark 10:30) I might be called father of manifold, holier children — or, to speak boundedly, hundredfold ones. And if there are fathers of whom it was said to Abraham, 'But thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace, nursed in a good old age' (Genesis 15:15) — one might say (I know not if truly) that those fathers perhaps once bore witness, leaving children — for which they became fathers of fathers: of the patriarch Abraham and other such patriarchs. For likely those who left children and bore witness become fathers not of babes but of fathers (Ephesians 3:15).
